Im thinking about buying it but I'm not sure. I havent played a big JRPG game since FFVII on the PS1. I want a similar experience, an immersive and emotional game set in a world that feels alive and beautiful. I've watched a few reviews, some positive and some negative. It seems like the kind of game that involves a lot of invested time. I like sinking a lot of time into a game but only if I fall in love with the world that the game is set in, otherwise I get bored and stop playing. Dark Souls was the last game that I felt engrossed in enough to play all the way through.

Anyone who has got it, what do you think? Are you enjoying the game? Can you give me some pros and cons? What does it feel like to explore the world?

If you're playing for the story XCX might not suit. You play as a player-made character, which always reduces the quality of the writing and the emotional investment in the main protagonist IMO (since you have to make a "everyman" character instead of an actual personality), but the affinity missions and your squadmates (especially Lin Lee who is fucking adorable) make up for this somewhat. The story is good.

But the world. Holy shit this world. It is amazing. As far as open world games go, this is one of the most amazing worlds I've ever seen. It's simply beautiful. I've put off story missions simply to go and explore and wander around and see what I can see, to try and climb mountains and look for treasure. It's amazing. If you're an explorer type of player on the Bartle Test, XCX will suit you to a tee.

It's hard for a game to hold my attention these days, but XCX is managing it just fine. I've had it less than a week and am already 35+ hours in to it and I have a giant freakin' robot.

Pros and Cons?

Pros:

Amazing world. Beautiful and vibrant and just wonderful.
Open world.
Some great characters and decent translation and writing.
Interesting plot for a game with a "make your own" main character.
So many systems! This game is deep and you can play without even scratching the surface if you want, but if you want to dive in to the details you could drown in them.
Absolutely beautiful. No Wii-U game has any right to look this good, considering the console hardware is basically over-clocked last-gen tech.

Cons

The systems, while varied, aren't explained very well in-game, requiring you to read the digital manual for some things, or search the internet for others.
Some mission objectives are vague, such as the "collect whatever" and they don't tell you where they can be found. Internet searches fix this but to me that feels like cheating.
It takes a long time to get a Skell (but the pay-off is absolutely worth it).

tl;dr, absolutely worth getting IMO. If not for The Witcher 3 it would be my GOTY hands-down.

It's long struck me that if I cut some text that into my clipboard, then go and copy or cut an object [say a file object] - shouldn't those two be kept both in the clipboard until the relevant contextual paste is applied?

In other words - I copy a folder name, then cut a file out of the folder - then go create a new folder, paste the folder name, then paste the file into the folder and the OS keeps track of the context of each object?

There's always been provision in the Windows clipboard to simultaneously copy multiple representations of data to the clipboard - for instance, if you copy some cells in Excel, it adds them in Excel's own format but also as CSV, so if you paste in Notepad it pastes as CSV and if you paste in Excel it keeps all the formatting etc.

Office also has multi-level clipboard functionality to let you cut and paste multiple things at once.

I think they avoided doing it fully automatically, though, because that could easily get really confusing. Let's say you have Word open, as well as Notepad. You select some text in Notepad and copy it. Then later you select some text in Word and try to paste that text into Notepad but you keep getting the text you originally copied from Notepad, not the new text that you've copied from Word (because it's ASCII and you're pasting ASCII but Word is copying formatted text.)

Unless I'm mistaken, OS/2 Presentation Manager circa the 3.0 days used to behave this way. There were some OO concepts implemented in that beast that were way ahead of their time, and which modern alternatives suckingly still lack 20 years later.
